c.tagline: Rugged harbour capital gateway to the world's last frontier.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are rarely used; agree on the fare with the driver before departing. Most visitors book taxis through their hotel for safety and fair pricing.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; hotels and tour operators usually have direct contacts for private security/medical assistance.

avoid.reason: Very high crime — carjacking and "raskol" gang robbery/violence; don’t walk, use hotel transport, avoid going out after dark; settlements are no-go

hood_desc: The compact colonial-era harbourfront core with government buildings, banks, Parliament Haus and the main port; convenient base for business travelers.

Port Moresby's main upmarket shopping and dining strip along the waterfront, with a public beach, yacht club and several of the city's better hotels; good for visitors wanting some walkable amenities.
A large government and commercial precinct built in the 1970s with Vision City Mall, ministries and mid-range hotels; practical but car-dependent.
A busy commercial and transit hub near the airport with markets and shopping centres, popular with business travelers needing airport proximity.
A quieter, leafy residential and diplomatic area near the airport with several secure hotels favoured by NGO staff, officials and longer-stay visitors.
lodging: The Sanctuary Hotel Resort and Spa

water.note: Reports on treatment quality are mixed; visitors should stick to bottled or boiled water.

transit.pay: Fares on PMVs and city buses are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in small kina amounts (typically K1-K3 per ride); there is no tap card or app-based ticketing system. Exact change is appreciated. Most visitors instead rely on hotel transport or pre-arranged taxis rather than public buses.
transit.hours: PMVs and buses generally run roughly 6am-6pm; little to no service after dark for safety reasons.
transit.note: Public transport is very basic and not recommended for tourists after dark; most visitors use hotel shuttles, arranged drivers, or taxis booked through their accommodation.

ferry: Coastal ferries to other PNG ports (e.g. Alotau, Lae) depart from Motukea/Port Moresby harbour, mainly for freight/regional travel rather than city transit

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in Papua New Guinea; a small tip for exceptional service is appreciated but not required.

food.name: Mumu
food.desc: The national feast: pork, chicken, kaukau and greens buried with hot stones in an earth oven lined with banana leaves and steamed for hours.

places.name: Aviat Club
places.note: Long-standing expat and local club that runs mumu-style buffets and PNG nights.

places.name: Airways Hotel
places.note: Stages traditional mumu and PNG buffet evenings on its terrace.

places.name: Ela Beach Hotel
places.note: Hotel buffets regularly feature mumu pork with kaukau and coconut greens.

food.name: Kokoda
food.desc: Raw reef fish or tuna cured in lime juice then folded through coconut cream with chilli, onion and tomato; Melanesian ceviche, served chilled.

places.name: Royal Papua Yacht Club

places.name: Duffy Cafe

food.name: Sago (Saksak)
food.desc: Starch pounded from the sago palm and cooked into stiff gelatinous dumplings or pancakes, often with grated coconut, banana or smoked fish.

places.name: Koki Market

places.name: Luluai
places.note: Local restaurant plating traditional starches with modern PNG dishes.

food.name: Aibika and Pumpkin Tips in Coconut Milk
food.desc: Kumu, the everyday PNG green: aibika leaves or pumpkin tips slow-simmered in coconut cream, eaten beside kaukau or rice at every meal.

places.name: Gordons Market
places.note: Bundles of aibika and pumpkin tips sold fresh every morning.

places.name: Aviat Club
places.note: Coconut-cooked greens are a fixture of its PNG buffet spread.

places.name: POM Restaurant
places.note: Kitchen focused on Papua New Guinean home cooking, greens included.

food.name: Koki Reef Fish and Mud Crab
food.desc: Barramundi, snapper and mangrove mud crab landed from the Gulf and Central coast, grilled simply over charcoal with lime and chilli.

places.name: Koki Fish Market
places.note: Stilt market over the water; buy the catch and have it cooked on the spot.

places.name: Royal Papua Yacht Club
places.note: Reliable grilled reef fish and crab in a secure waterfront setting.

places.name: Ribito Grill and Restaurant
places.note: Grill house working with PNG flavours and local seafood.

food.name: Kai Bar Chicken and Lamb Flaps
food.desc: The street staple: fried chicken, greasy lamb flaps and scones sold by the piece from counter-fronted kai bars, eaten with rice.

places.name: Boroko kai bars

places.name: Vision City Mega Mall food court

places.name: Gordons Market surrounds

food.name: PNG Highlands Coffee
food.desc: Arabica grown in the Wahgi and Waghi valleys above 1,500m; bright, fruity and roasted locally, and one of the country's proudest exports.

places.name: Duffy Cafe

places.name: Edge Cafe

places.name: Grand Papua Hotel lobby cafe

food.name: SP Lager
food.desc: South Pacific Lager, brewed in Port Moresby since 1952 and the unofficial national drink; the green bottle is everywhere from clubs to markets.

places.name: Royal Papua Yacht Club
places.note: Sunset SP on the marina deck is a Port Moresby ritual.

places.name: Aviat Club

places.name: Lamana Hotel

landmarks: Bomana War Cemetery
A solemn, immaculately kept WWII cemetery honoring thousands of Allied soldiers, one of the most moving sites in the Pacific.
Parliament Haus
PNG's National Parliament building, designed in the style of a traditional Sepik 'haus tambaran' spirit house, is the country's most distinctive piece of architecture.
Ela Beach
A palm-fringed city beach along Port Moresby's waterfront, popular for sunset views over the harbor.
Owers' Corner (Kokoda Track trailhead)
The historic starting point of the famed WWII Kokoda Track, framed by dramatic Owen Stanley Range scenery.
Hanuabada Village
An iconic stilt village of Motu houses built out over the harbor, offering a striking glimpse of traditional coastal life beside the modern capital.
Port Moresby Nature Park
A lush botanical and wildlife park showcasing PNG's birds of paradise, orchids, and other unique flora and fauna.
APEC Haus
A striking, sail-shaped waterfront building built for the 2018 APEC summit, inspired by a traditional lakatoi outrigger canoe.
National Museum and Art Gallery of PNG
Home to an extensive collection of traditional PNG artifacts, masks, and canoes representing the country's hundreds of distinct cultures.
Varirata National Park
PNG's first national park, perched on a plateau above the city with rainforest trails, birds of paradise, and sweeping coastal views.
Loloata Island
A small resort island just off the coast renowned for its coral reefs and WWII wreck diving in clear tropical waters.

train.note: Papua New Guinea has no passenger railways. Port Moresby is also not connected by road to Lae or any other major town, so long-distance travel within the country is almost entirely by air.

bus.note: No international coaches. Within Port Moresby and Central Province, informal PMVs (public motor vehicles - shared minibuses) are the local buses, but because the capital has no road link to the rest of PNG there is no intercity coach network; use flights to reach Lae, Mount Hagen and other centres.

ferry.note: No scheduled international passenger ferries from Port Moresby. Domestic coastal shipping serves some ports, but the reliable link between Port Moresby and the rest of the country is air travel (Air Niugini, PNG Air). Passenger ships in PNG mostly operate out of Lae and Rabaul, not the capital.
